layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The effect of the nickel content on the pitting resistance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 304 stainless steel (SS) and Alloys

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 800 and 600 in chloride-thiosulfate solutions was investigated using two techniques, scratching and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: slow-stepped potentiostatic polarization. Adverse effects of nickel were seen at both low and high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thiosulfate concentrations. For a constant chloride concentration at 24 and 80 C the pitting potential (Ep)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: exhibited a minimum value with the change in thiosulfate concentration. At this minimum, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semi-logarithmic relation prevailed between the nickel content and the ratio of the chloride-thiosulfate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentrations. With the nickel addition, the alloy became susceptible to larger concentration ratios and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a tenfold increase in ratio occurred between AISI 304 SS and Alloy 600. The maximum decrease in Ep

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recorded at 80 C going from chloride to chloride-thiosulfate solutions amounted to 550, 625, and 700

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mV for AISI 304 SS, Alloy 800, and Alloy 600 respectively. This decrease suggests that the presence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of thiosulfate may account for some of the failures that have occurred with AISI 304 SS and Alloy 800

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: when used as tubing materials in fresh water-cooled heat exchangers.

layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The resistance of stainless alloys to generalized corrosion is pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vided by the growth of a thin oxide film. In aqueous solutions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: however, impurities can locally destroy this passive layer and render

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the alloys susceptible to localized corrosion. Thiosulfate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been recognized as a potentially aggressive anion for several years

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: now and various forms of localized corrosion having far-reaching

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consequences in the nuclear, petroleum, and pulp and paper

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: industries have been detected and studied for a range of stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels (SSs). Thus, AISI 304 SS and Alloy 600, both sensitized, were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found susceptible to stress corrosion cracking in thiosulfate solu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions.1-5 Although for pitting and crevice corrosion, the thiosulfate ion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: itself was not found to be aggressive to SSs, in combination with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride and sulfate ions it has proved extremely deleterious. Pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions have been studied by Newman and collaborators6,7and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Garner® for a pure FeCrNi alloy, AISI 304, 316, and 317L SSs, while

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tromansº extended his crevice corrosion work to AISI 904L SS.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In his studies of the pitting of SS in thiosulfate solutions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing chloride or sulfate ions, Newman suggested that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thiosulfate ion was an activating species in the anodic dissolution of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nickel. From the reduction of the thiosulfates in the pit nuclei,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adsorbed sulfur (or sulfide) is produced on the bare metal surface

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thus hindering the repassivation processes. Newman paralleled this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavior with the known effect of adsorbed sulfur on FeNi alloys.1º

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Following sulfur adsorption, the usual pitting mechanism occurs with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the hydrolysis of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions and the decrease in pH to a value low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enough to sustain the very high rate of anodic dissolution. Garner

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found that very small additions (5 to 20 ppm) of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to a standard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paper-machine white water (100 ppm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at 4.5 pH and 50 C) with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or without chloride could pit AISI 304 SS and that an increase to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: neutral pH had very little effect on the thiosulfate attack. Both authors

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: agree that alloying with molybdenum renders the alloy more resistant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to pitting under thiosulfate conditions. So far, no study has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: made of thiosulfate pitting of more highly alloyed nickel materials.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: An area where the pitting of molybdenum-free stainless mate-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rials is often attributed to simple chloride ions is in natural water. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fact, AISI 304 SS, when used as a material for heat exchanger tubing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in such conditions, is well known to pit. More recently, Alloy 800,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: although it contains roughly four times the nickel content of AISl 304

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SS, was also found susceptible to pitting attack in fresh water-cooled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: heat exchangers.11 It cannot be excluded a priori, however, that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presence of small amounts of thiosulfates in the water in contact with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the tubes may have caused the observed effect on those alloys.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Indeed, suitable conditions exist for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: production, whether from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hydrogen sulfide or metallic sulfide under oxygenated conditions,12.13

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or as an intermediate species under anaerobic conditions in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reduction of sulfates by microorganisms.14

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Based on the aforementioned studies and observations, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: present work was undertaken to investigate the effect of nickel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additions on the thiosulfate pitting of SSs. It was expected that,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: according to the proposed mechanism of sulfur adsorption and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhanced anodic dissolution of nickel, an increase in the nickel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content would somehow affect the pitting behavior. A low-level

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride solution typical of natural fresh water was chosen as a base

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution and various amounts of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were added. The materials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selected, AISI 304 SS, Alloy 800, and Alloy 600, are of practical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interest due to the range of nickel content they offer.A scratching

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Electrochemical impedance (AC impedance) measurements are practical for predicting corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavior. Combining this technique with small amplitude DC polarization offers a rapid method of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: estimating corrosion rates. Optimization of the potentiostat gain allows for the rapid estimation of very

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low corrosion rates. Full use of this technique in predicting corrosion behavior is achieved by using a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: microcomputer to control data acquisition and a mainframe computer for data analysis. Successful use

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of this combination to estimate low corrosion rates and to determine other types of corrosion behavior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is demonstrated for several practical applications. These applications are rapid estimation of passive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy corrosion and evaluation of inhibitors of carbon steel corrosion in neutral pH water.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Electrochemical impedance (AC impedance) measurements have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been gaining increasing favor for making practical corrosion predic-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions. A number of reviews have been written that discuss both the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: theory and many areas of application.1-3 These reviews suggest that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two areas of application are rapid estimates of a wide range of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion rates and practical insights into corrosion mechanisms,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: especially in the presence of an adsorbed film or an applied organic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coating. Other applications have been reported. Either their reduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to practice is not as well developed or the application has less

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relevance to the immediate need.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The use of electrochemical impedance for corrosion rate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: estimation is well established. In its simplest form, the method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires two steps. The frequency response of the corroding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrode is used to obtain the polarization or charge transfer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance. The current vs voltage curve obtained by DC polarization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is then used to estimate the Tafel slopes. Finally, the corrosion rate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is obtained through the equation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: areas) and there is one dominant charge transfer reaction that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: controls corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: There have been a number of studies that show that Equations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) and (2) can be used very effectively to estimate corrosion rates.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For example, Mansfeld has used Equation (1) to estimate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion rate of iron in 0.5 M sulfuric acid in the absence and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presence of inhibitors.4 The corrosion rates were fairly high, 25 mm/y

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for iron in sulfuric acid and ~0.025 to 0.25 mm/y in inhibited sulfuric

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acid. More recently, Williams and Asher reported that the electro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chemical impedance technique could be used to estimate extremely

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low corrosion rates, of the order of 500 nm/y to 1 μm/y.⁵ This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: development has tremendous importance for application in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chemical process industries. The acceptability of an alloy is increas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ingly being dictated not by gross corrosion but by contamination.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Corrosion rates as low as 1 to 2 μm/y might be unacceptable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: because of fluid contamination by metal ions created by the corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: process. This corrosion rate is barely measurable by traditional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 30-day coupon immersion tests. Therefore, one area of interest is the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: estimation of low corrosion rates by electrochemical impedance. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy is at least comparable to if not better than estimates from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 30-day immersion tests. Electrochemical impedance estimates are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: available in far less time.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The second area of application is to evaluate inhibitors,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: especially for water treatment. The use of electrochemical imped-
